Morning Brief
Nifty 50 was flat at 22,750 with broad buying, 1,822 advancers to 718 decliners
Today’s read
The biggest names carried the session. The fifty most traded stocks returned +2.62% weighted by turnover, against +1.31% for the median stock, a gap of 1.3 percentage points, so most stocks did worse than the busiest names suggest.

Brigade Hotel Ventures Limited rose 2.1% on 55 times its usual volume. Its exchange filing that session was about guidance or investor update, “Investor Presentation”.

Tata Teleservices (Maharashtra) Limited rose 0.8% on 53 times its usual volume, and it was in the news with “Stocks in news: Jio Platforms, RIL, Infosys, L&T, Tata Capital, Waaree Energies and Vedanta Iron”.

Seshasayee Paper and Boards Limited fell 9.9% on 60 times its usual volume, and it was in the news with “Atyant Capital sells 2.73% stake in Seshasayee Paper; MSTC, Advit Jewels see bulk deals”.

Nothing in the news or in exchange filings explains the volume in Vinyl Chemicals (India) Limited (86x), Shiv Aum Steels Limited (82x), Pashupati Cotspin Limited (70x). That usually points to a sector story rather than a company one.

What happened
Breaking
Fed likely to wait on another rate hike as inflation pressures mount - coastalabc.com
U.S. Federal Reserve officials signaled interest rates will stay elevated as sticky inflation delays monetary easing. Higher U.S. treasury yields widen interest rate differentials, driving foreign portfolio equity outflows from India and pressuring the rupee. This domestic liquidity squeeze restricts the Reserve Bank of India from cutting repo rates, weighing on valuation multiples for rate-sensitive banking and real estate stocks.
Fed and rates
India should not deplete reserves to defend rupee, ex-RBI chief Rajan says
Former RBI Governor Raghuram Rajan advised the central bank against spending foreign exchange reserves to artificially support the rupee. Allowing gradual currency depreciation enhances export price competitiveness for IT services and pharmaceutical firms. However, a weaker rupee raises landed costs for imported crude oil, compressing operating margins for paint companies, specialty chemical manufacturers, and oil marketing companies.

Infosys draws four downgrades in a day on weaker annual sales outlook
Four brokerages downgraded Infosys following a downward revision in its annual sales guidance due to weak discretionary technology spending. Slower deal conversions compress billable employee utilization rates across large-cap IT services firms, including TCS, Wipro, and HCLTech. The guidance cut signals revenue drag across the IT sector, threatening earnings estimates and prompting valuation de-ratings.

Atyant Capital offloaded a 2.73% equity stake in Seshasayee Paper and Boards through open market bulk sales. Secondary fund transactions do not alter underlying operational fundamentals, paper demand, or gross margins for the company. The sale increases short-term share supply overhead without changing long-term earnings drivers. Next quarter pulp price trends will determine near-term margin expansion.

Jakson Solar to invest INR 50 billion in 3 GW solar cell and ingot-wafer plants - Prop News Time
Unlisted Jakson Solar announced a 50 billion rupee capital expenditure to establish a 3 GW integrated solar cell and ingot-wafer facility. Expanding domestic upstream component capacity reduces reliance on Chinese imports under government trade protections. Increased domestic manufacturing capacity expands business opportunities for listed solar ancillary suppliers, capital goods providers, and EPC contractors including Borosil Renewables and Tata Power.

Amazon stock target raised by Morgan Stanley, UBS ahead of Q3 results; what are the key catalysts? Know here
Morgan Stanley and UBS raised Amazon price targets on expectations of accelerating AWS cloud growth, offset by elevated AI capital expenditures. Stronger AWS momentum signals resilient enterprise technology spending, benefiting Indian IT service exporters like TCS, Infosys, and HCLTech through cloud migration deal execution. Q3 cloud revenue growth rate figures from AWS will confirm whether enterprise discretionary IT spending is recovering.

Defence stocks rally: Apollo Micro Systems, Data Patterns, BEML, HAL, BEL surge as DAC clears acquisition push, Aequs & Mazagon Dock slump after Q2
The Defence Acquisition Council granted preliminary approvals for military procurement proposals, expanding order pipelines for defence suppliers like HAL, BEL, and Data Patterns. These clearances improve long-term order book visibility, supporting valuation multiples across the sector despite near-term Q2 margin pressures seen at shipbuilders like Mazagon Dock. Conversion of these approvals into definitive contracts over the next two quarters will validate revenue realization.

India’s Defense Exports to Europe Surge Amid Increased Military Spending - SSBCrack
European defense spending increases have driven higher export demand for Indian military hardware, broadening the addressable market for manufacturers like Bharat Forge and Solar Industries. Higher export volumes carry superior operating margins relative to domestic public sector procurement, enhancing overall EBITDA margins. Quarterly export revenue disclosures in upcoming financial filings will confirm the magnitude of European contract execution.
Defence indigenisation
Wall Street ends higher on revived AI momentum
US equity markets closed higher as buyers returned to megacap technology stocks following strong artificial intelligence spending plans. This risk-on sentiment supports valuation multiples for Indian IT exporters such as TCS, Infosys, and HCLTech by easing fears of immediate client spending cuts. Sustained US tech earnings growth will determine whether foreign portfolio investors continue allocating capital to Indian equities this quarter.
Reuters Business
Bond market doubts gridlock will ease deficit woes this time
US Treasury yields held firm near recent highs as bond markets priced in structural fiscal deficits regardless of election outcomes. Higher US yields narrow the interest rate differential with India, putting downward pressure on the rupee and slowing foreign portfolio debt inflows. A breakout in the US ten-year yield above 4.50 percent would confirm tightening financial conditions for Indian corporate borrowers.

India considers measures to boost local production of 100 critical inputs to cut import reliance, government official says
India identified 100 high-reliance import items, concentrated in active pharmaceutical ingredients, chemicals, and capital goods, for targeted domestic manufacturing support. The initiative aims to protect gross margins and operating stability for listed API makers and specialty chemical firms like Divi's Laboratories and SRF. Policy details specifying capital subsidies or production-linked incentives will reveal the actual earnings impact over the medium term.

US Fed opens two-day meeting with markets expecting rate hold
The US Federal Reserve opened its policy meeting with markets pricing a near-ninety percent chance of holding interest rates steady. A prolonged rate hold maintains high global borrowing costs, restricting the Reserve Bank of India's room to cut repo rates and dampening interest-rate-sensitive sectors like housing and autos. Updated dot plot projections will confirm whether foreign portfolio inflows resume before the quarter ends.

Big Tech earnings to test AI boom amid market turmoil
US Big Tech companies are raising combined annual AI capital expenditures past $200 billion in upcoming Q3 filings. This enterprise infrastructure spending directly feeds contract pipelines for Indian IT services majors like TCS, Infosys, and Wipro, which implement cloud and AI integrations. Management commentary on client discretionary IT budgets will confirm whether these capex commitments translate into broader deal wins.
Reuters Business · +1 other
JSW Infrastructure Q2 Results: Net profit falls 11% to Rs 328 crore
JSW Infrastructure's Q2 consolidated net profit fell 11% year-on-year to Rs 328.23 crore, as total expenses surged 18% to Rs 1,238.34 crore despite top-line growth. Operating margins contracted due to higher depreciation and finance costs from recent port capacity additions, highlighting near-term margin pressure for port operators. Second-half cargo volume growth figures will confirm whether asset utilization can absorb these fixed costs.

Visa results beat estimates as resilient customers keep up spending
Visa posted Q4 adjusted earnings of $2.71 per share on $9.6 billion in revenue, driven by an 8% increase in payment volume and a 13% surge in cross-border transactions. Strong international consumer spending supports transaction fee growth and credit card issuance revenues for Indian private lenders like HDFC Bank and ICICI Bank. Monthly RBI data on outbound credit card spend will confirm if domestic trends match this global travel resilience.

China Stock Premium Over Hong Kong Widens on State Intervention
Beijing state-backed buying pushed the Hang Seng China AH Premium Index to a 17-month high, widening the valuation gap between onshore A-shares and offshore H-shares. The discount on Hong Kong equities risks diverting foreign portfolio flows away from high-multiple Indian benchmarks toward cheaper offshore Chinese assets. Daily foreign institutional investor net sales in Indian cash markets will confirm whether global allocators execute this tactical shift.
